#  | DMM + zurg + rex

> Guides and reference for Debrid Media Manager, zurg and rex: set up a debrid or Usenet library and play it in Plex, Jellyfin, Emby and other apps.

- [Notes](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/index.md): Notes
- [zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/index.md): zurg puts your debrid accounts and Usenet library in one virtual folder. It stores no local video. Nothing is fetched until a player asks for it. A 60 GB remux does not use 60 GB of local disk.
- [rex](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/index.md): rex is a media server for the official Plex apps that owns no files. A source tells it what is in your library and serves each file. rex streams that file when you press play.
- [DMM](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/dmm/index.md): Debrid Media Manager helps you find movies and shows and keep them in your debrid library.
- [Guides](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/index.md): Every guide for DMM, zurg and rex in one list: choosing a setup, getting help, sponsorship and each project's how-tos.

## zurg

### Setup

- [Setup](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/setup/index.md): The binary installer is the shortest path on Linux, macOS and Windows. Docker remains available on a Linux host when a container fits better. Docker
- [Linux binary setup](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/setup/linux.md): The optional sponsor bootstrap installs system packages downloads the right CPU build and runs setup and diagnostics:
- [Docker setup](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/setup/docker.md): This guide runs zurg in Docker and exposes its FUSE mount on a Linux host. Docker supplies zurg rclone and ffprobe. The built-in setup command creates the config.
- [macOS Tutorial](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/setup/macos.md): The optional sponsor bootstrap installs macFUSE when needed downloads the Intel or Apple silicon build and runs the provider chooser and diagnostics:
- [Windows, the binary, from scratch](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/setup/windows.md): Run the optional sponsor bootstrap from PowerShell. It installs WinFsp through UAC downloads zurg and runs the provider chooser and diagnostics:

### Providers

- [Providers](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/providers/index.md): A provider is one account zurg builds its library from. Every account is one entry under providers: in config.yml. Run one account or run six. A release held by more than one of them is listed once and read from whichever account can serve it at the time.
- [Real-Debrid](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/providers/realdebrid.md): Use a Real-Debrid account with zurg: get the API token, add it to config.yml and see what zurg does with Real-Debrid.
- [TorBox](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/providers/torbox.md): Use a TorBox account with zurg: get the API key, add it to config.yml and see how zurg stays within TorBox's limits.
- [AllDebrid](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/providers/alldebrid.md): Use an AllDebrid account with zurg: get the API key, add it to config.yml and see how zurg lists and streams AllDebrid files.
- [Premiumize](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/providers/premiumize.md): Use a Premiumize account with zurg: get the API key, add it to config.yml and mount both transfers and cloud files.
- [Debrid-Link](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/providers/debridlink.md): Use a Debrid-Link account with zurg: get the API key, add it to config.yml and see how zurg keeps the seedbox in sync.
- [Offcloud](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/providers/offcloud.md): Use an Offcloud account with zurg: get the API key, add it to config.yml and see how zurg lists and checks Offcloud files.
- [Usenet](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/providers/usenet.md): Stream Usenet with zurg: drop NZB files in a watch folder and zurg plays them straight from your news server, nothing downloaded first.
- [TorBox hosted Usenet](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/providers/torbox-nzb.md): Let TorBox fetch your Usenet releases for zurg: post NZB files to a TorBox Pro account and play them with no news server of your own.
- [TorBox limits and how zurg adapts to them](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/providers/torbox-limits.md): zurg's library behaviour grew around Real-Debrid's constraints. TorBox's are different in kind, not just in magnitude, and driving it like Real-Debrid gets the account rate-limited within seconds of a first library scan.
- [TorBox news server](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/providers/torbox-news-server.md): A TorBox Pro subscription bundles a Usenet account. It is a real NNTP server and zurg can use it as an ordinary type: nzb provider. This page records what that server is and what it is worth as a provider slot.
- [ElfHosted news server](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/providers/elfhosted-news-server.md): ElfHosted bundles a Usenet account with its Stremio addon plans and calls it Usenet Essential. This page records what that server is. Everything below was measured on 2026-09-04 from one host.

### Guides

- [Guides](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/index.md): Working with the library: Usenet, the arrs, __magic__, and media servers. rex has its own section.
- [Usenet with zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/usenet.md): zurg's nzb backend turns .nzb files into a mounted library. There is no downloader or completed folder. Nothing is downloaded before play. It stores the NZBs and bounded caches in data/bytecache and data/par2 plus index records.
- [Sonarr and Radarr, step by step](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/sonarr-radarr.md): There are three ways to use Sonarr and Radarr with zurg. Choose who searches zurg or the *arrs. See which one to pick.
- [Sonarr and Radarr with torrents, step by step](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/sonarr-radarr-torrents.md): There are three ways to use Sonarr and Radarr with zurg. The real choice is who searches, zurg or the *arrs: which one to pick compares them.
- [Let zurg fetch what Sonarr and Radarr want](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/sonarr-radarr-fetch.md): There are three ways to use Sonarr and Radarr with zurg. The real choice is who searches, zurg or the *arrs: which one to pick compares them.
- [Following a list in Sonarr and Radarr](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/import-lists.md): Sonarr and Radarr can follow a list of shows or movies. Every title on it gets added and searched. With zurg as the download client each grab lands on your debrid account and imports into __magic__ like any other.
- [Subtitles with Bazarr](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/subtitles.md): Bazarr finds subtitles for what Sonarr and Radarr import and saves each one next to its video. With zurg the video sits in __magic__, and so does the subtitle.
- [Whisparr](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/whisparr.md): Whisparr is Radarr for adult films and scenes. It uses zurg as its qBittorrent client. Grabs go to your debrid account. Importing only renames a path inside __magic__; nothing is downloaded or copied.
- [__magic__, a directory you can organise](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/magic.md): Every other zurg directory is computed. movies applies the movies filter. __all__ holds everything. A release folder holds what the account reports. The layout is rebuilt on each refresh.
- [Renaming releases and files](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/renaming.md): zurg's mount is writable in exactly one way: you can rename a release folder or a file inside one, anywhere in the library. It is on by default. Nothing is
- [Plex Features & Capabilities](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/plex.md): Running rex beside Plex Media Server, or instead of it? Move from Plex to rex says what to keep in zurg, your rclone mount included, and which of zurg's Plex settings to remove.
- [Acquisition sources](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/acquisition.md): Plex watchlist your DMM wanted list Seerr Radarr and Sonarr use one acquisition engine. It tracks progress retries and acknowledgement. Newznab results become NZBs for zurg's Usenet backend.
- [Plex watchlist acquisition](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/plex-watchlist.md): Plex watchlist is an adapter on the shared acquisition engine, alongside Seerr. Existing watchlist.enabled and legacy Plex watchlist settings keep working. The adapter resolves cloud-watchlist titles and hands them to the shared executor.
- [Fetch what you want from DMM](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/dmm-wanted.md): Press Want on a film or show on Debrid Media Manager, and your zurg fetches it. There is no Sonarr or Radarr to set up and nothing to mount. Shows keep getting their new episodes as they air.
- [The Stremio addon](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/stremio.md): zurg can answer Stremio as an addon. Stremio asks by IMDb id. zurg searches your Newznab indexers and pulls the chosen release's NZB into the Usenet backend.
- [Jellyfin Features & Capabilities](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/jellyfin.md): Config keys (config.md, config.example.yml): jellyfin_server_url (string, default ), jellyfin_token (string, default ). Both ship commented out in config.example.yml and are absent from config.simple.yml.
- [Local debrid libraries and portable zurgtorrents](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/local-libraries.md): A local library takes its membership from portable .zurgtorrent files. It appears in the normal WebDAV, HTTP and provider directories. Importing files, listing them and refreshing the catalog do not add torrents or resolve download links.
- [zurg+rex for Android and Google TV](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/guides/android.md): The Android app runs a zurg engine on the device and rex beside it: your own Plex server on your phone or TV box, for the Plex apps. One app works on phones tablets Android TV and Google TV.

### Migrating

- [Migrating to zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/migrate/index.md): Read this page first. It applies to every migration and it is most of what you need. The per-server pages are short because this one carries the shared part.
- [Migrating from AltMount to zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/migrate/altmount.md): Read the shared page first. It explains the trash guard and why your library lands in __magic__.
- [Migrating from decypharr to zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/migrate/decypharr.md): Read the shared page first. It explains the trash guard and why your library lands in __magic__.
- [Migrating from InfiniDysk to zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/migrate/infinidysk.md): Read the shared page first. It explains the trash guard and why your library lands in __magic__.
- [Migrating from nzbdav to zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/migrate/nzbdav.md): Read the shared page first. It explains the trash guard and why your library lands in __magic__.
- [Migrating from streamnzb v5.1.0 to zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/migrate/streamnzb.md): streamnzb is a Stremio addon. It searches Newznab indexers when you press play and streams the winner. Nothing is kept. It has no filesystem WebDAV mount or Plex library.

### Reference

- [Reference](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/reference/index.md): Look-up pages. Nothing here is a walkthrough. Read them when you know what you want and need the exact name of it.
- [zurg Configuration Documentation](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/reference/config.md): This document details all available configuration options for zurg. Configure these options in your config.yml file.
- [Command line](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/reference/cli.md): The zurg binary is the server and a set of tools. Run it with no command to start the server. Every command takes --help and prints the text this page is written from.
- [zurg Tags Documentation](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/reference/tags.md): This document describes all possible tags that can be automatically applied to torrents in zurg.
- [The MCP endpoint](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/reference/mcp.md): zurg can answer an AI agent over the Model Context Protocol: the client asks what tools exist, zurg describes them, and the agent calls them to read the library, work out why a release is not playing, repair it, or drive the media servers.
- [Outbound request identity](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/reference/outbound-identity.md): user_agent controls the shared HTTP User-Agent for debrid APIs and CDN reads, Newznab searches, NZB downloads, OpenSubtitles, ffprobe probes, media-server integrations, dependency downloads, updates and optional sharing/log exports.
- [Changelog](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/reference/changelog.md): A Sonarr source used to skip a daily series, an anime series and a series' specials, with one warning each. Now a daily show's missing episodes are also

### Internals

- [Internals](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/internals/index.md): How zurg is built. What it was measured at. The design notes behind the awkward parts. Written for someone about to change the code. Nothing here is needed to run zurg.
- [Architecture](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/internals/architecture.md): A map of what zurg is, how the pieces fit, and why each package exists. Aimed at someone about to change the code: it names the load-bearing decisions and the invariants that are easy to break without noticing.
- [Persistent read caches](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/internals/persistent-caches.md): Imported NZBs, Real-Debrid, AllDebrid and TorBox entries all retain their library state in data/*.zurgtorrent. These files describe the library. Read
- [The debrid baseline](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/internals/debrid-baseline.md): What zurg costs and how fast it feels on the debrid path — Real-Debrid, AllDebrid and TorBox. There is no competitor here. The contender is a later zurg, and this file is what it has to beat.
- [Torrent lifecycle on Real-Debrid AllDebrid and TorBox](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/internals/torrent-lifecycle.md): Measured on 2026-08-30 against live accounts. Everything below marked observed came out of a capture. Everything marked inferred did not and says why.
- [qBittorrent Web API contract as consumed by Sonarr and Radarr (develop)](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/internals/qbittorrent-client-contract.md): Source of truth: files fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com/{Sonarr/Sonarr,Radarr/Radarr}/develop/... and from qbittorrent/qBittorrent/master on 2026-08-27.
- [zurg naming](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/internals/naming.md): Almost every name zurg shows is computed, never stored. A release's folder name, a file's name inside it, and the on-disk filename of its cache record are all derived from the torrent on every lookup.
- [SABnzbd API contract as consumed by Sonarr and Radarr (develop)](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/internals/sabnzbd-client-contract.md): Source of truth: files fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com/{Sonarr/Sonarr,Radarr/Radarr}/develop/... on 2026-08-22. Every line number below was read out of those files.
- [Aligning the Plex trash sweep with zurg's own file status](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/internals/plex-trash-sweep.md): The Plex trash sweep currently decides what to remove from a Plex library using file absence plus an age timer. zurg already knows something far better — whether the content behind that file is repairable or permanently dead — and does not consult it.
- [Proxied stream timeout regression](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/internals/stream-timeout-regression.md): zurg used download_timeout_secs as a wall-clock deadline for proxied HTTP downloads. Its default is 15 seconds, so any single upstream response whose body took longer than 15 seconds to finish was cut off even while bytes were arriving normally.
- [Empty imports after a refused move](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/internals/rclone-move-refusal.md): Reproduced with rclone 1.72.0, a local-first union, VFS full caching and the .NET 6 File.Move(source, destination) used by Sonarr 4.0.19.2979.
- [Directory Configuration UI/UX Assessment](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/internals/uiux.md): Page: Directory Configuration at http://localhost:9999/directories/.
- [E2E Testing](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/internals/e2e-test.md): End-to-end tests to verify zurg is working correctly after deployment.
- [Torrents](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/zurg/internals/realdebrid-behavior.md): Real-debrid supports downloading unlimited number of torrent files and magnet links, also selecting which files in it that you want to download If the

## rex

- [rex questions](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/faq.md): Short answers to what people ask before they install rex, and soon after. Each answer links to the guide that has the details.
- [rex with your own app](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/any-source.md): rex is a media server for the official Plex apps that owns no files. The official Plex apps see it as a normal Plex server. Another program, which this page calls your app, tells rex what is in your library and serves the files.
- [rex with your Stremio addons](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/stremio.md): rex-stremio turns Stremio addon catalogs into rex libraries. Films shows and live channels then play in Plex apps. Nothing is downloaded. When someone presses play rex-stremio asks the stream addon for a link and rex plays it.
- [rex with zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/with-zurg.md): rex is a media server for the official Plex apps that owns no files. The official Plex apps see it as a normal Plex server. Any app can fill it (rex with
- [Live TV with rex](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/live-tv.md): rex shows addon channels in Plex Web and Plex for Android's Live TV with a guide and What's On. Pick a channel and it plays at once. rex-live-sports is ready to use with a live-sports server.
- [Music with rex](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/music.md): rex can hold a music library for Plexamp Plex Web and Plex for Android. A music addon sends each song and its MusicBrainz release. Plex fills in names covers artist details genres and similar artists.
- [Move from Plex to rex](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/from-plex.md): You run Plex Media Server and want to try rex. Your Plex apps stay the same. The library source and server address change.
- [Share rex with family and friends](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/sharing.md): Share rex from its registered account through Plex's Manage Library Access. Each person signs in to Plex as themselves and sees rex beside their other servers with their own watch history.
- [Bring your watch history to rex](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/import-watched.md): rex starts with no watch history. It can copy watched titles resume points and star ratings from another Plex server. Watched titles stay watched. Part-watched titles return to Continue Watching.
- [Building rex addons](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/addons.md): rex shows what its sources tell it about. A source tells rex what it has through the feed API and serves the files when rex asks. rex treats every source the same.
- [Tutorial: a home videos addon](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/addon-home-videos.md): This tutorial builds a rex addon in one Python file. It puts your phone clips camcorder files or screen recordings into a Home Videos library in every Plex app.
- [Tutorial: a music addon](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/addon-music.md): This tutorial puts a folder of albums into a Music library that Plexamp Plex Web and Plex for Android play. It supports FLAC MP3 AAC and other common files. Your files stay where they are.
- [Tutorial: an IPTV addon](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/addon-iptv.md): This tutorial turns an IPTV playlist (M3U) and TV guide (XMLTV) into Live TV channels in Plex Web and Plex for Android. Each channel keeps its number and guide.
- [More from your addon](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/addon-more.md): Building rex addons covers the basics. This page adds subtitles trailers chapters collections playlists artist pictures known films large libraries fixes and removal.
- [Kometa with rex](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/kometa.md): Kometa builds collections, puts badges on posters (4K, HDR, ratings) and fills in ratings and genres on a Plex server. rex answers Kometa the way a Plex server does, so the same config works on your rex libraries.
- [Apps download from your provider](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/rex/direct-download.md): Normally rex reads every movie from your source and passes it to Plex. If the source returns a file link such as a debrid download link rex can hand it to Plex.

## DMM

- [Seerr through DMM](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/dmm/seerr.md): Add DMM to Seerr as Radarr and Sonarr. Approved requests land on your DMM wanted list for zurg to fetch. You do not need Radarr or Sonarr. Seerr only needs to reach debridmediamanager.com.
- [DMM buttons in Safari](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/dmm/safari.md): The DMM browser extension puts a DMM🔎 button on movie and TV sites. It opens the title on DMM. Next to magnet links it adds a DMM🧲 button that adds the torrent to your DMM library.

## Guides

- [Which setup should I use?](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/choose-your-setup.md): Find your setup with the interactive questionnaire. Answer a few questions about your player accounts and hosting. It returns routes requirements and setup links.
- [What a sponsorship gives you](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/sponsorship.md): DMM is free. Sponsorships pay for its hosting and keep zurg and rex moving. This page lists every perk and where to set it up.
- [Getting help with zurg and rex](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/remote-help.md): Post in the Discord forum for what you use: zurg-support rex-support or dmm-support. Open one thread per problem. Say what you did what you expected and what happened.
